generation: Trinity Advanced Pro / Advanced Pro TT (rim brake, MY2016-2024)
identify: Rim brakes integrated behind the fork and under the frame, AeroVault front bottle on the fork/head tube, two separate armrest stacks bolted on top of an AeroDrive base bar that sits on a Giant-only nose-cone stem (flat or +30 mm). Launched late 2015 as MY16; replaced by the disc Trinity Advanced SL in Jan 2025. NOT the cheaper Trinity Advanced (non-Pro), which has a normal stem and base-bar clamp, and NOT the 2011-2015 'Trinity Advanced SL'.

cockpit.steerer: Alloy OverDrive steerer on a composite fork (Giant spec); the stem and lower nose cone are Giant-specific and paired, so a standard stem cannot be clamped on per owners.
cockpit.stem: Proprietary Giant Trinity stem / nose cone, 80 mm long in the 2020-2022 tables (a 2018 table lists 80/90/90/100 mm by size). Complete bikes shipped with two alloy stems: zero stack and +30 mm. TT/UCI and Tri stems differ in height, angle and fasteners.
cockpit.pad_bolt_spacing: About 30 mm centre-to-centre between the two armrest bolts (one owner's measurement, 2017); not published by Giant.
cockpit.stack_system: Armrest spacer stack under each armrest/extension clamp, bolted with long M5 bolts (stock lengths M5 x 40/50/60/70 per the Giant manual as quoted by an owner). Giant's 2022 tables give a 60 mm pad-stack range for the Tri setup and 50 mm for TT. Base bar is reversible (Giant: 40 mm of height adjustment) and the +30 mm stem raises the whole front end. Owners go beyond the stock range with extra Giant spacers and longer bolts; a Giant armrest bridge is advised for tall stacks.
cockpit.reach_system: Armrests bolt onto the extension clamps in four positions and can be reversed for five fore-aft positions in 15 mm steps, 60 mm in total (Giant manual, via search excerpt). No alternative stem lengths sold separately apart from the TT/UCI kit.
cockpit.angle_system: none stock. Owners add angled spacers (Fouriers 10/15 deg) or AeroCoach tilt-block adapters. One owner measured the stock extension clamps tilting about 2 deg nose-down on the risers.
cockpit.notes: Fit range is narrow; owners report not getting long and low enough on small sizes even with spacers removed. Stock extensions are standard round bars and owners swapped them freely; the base bar and stem are Giant-only. The stem-to-fork bolt and stack-spacer threads strip if over-tightened (owner reports). A basebar break after a small impact and a crash crack were each reported once.

effect.text: Swaps the zero-stack stem for the +30 mm one, lifting base bar and pads about 30 mm (owners estimate about an inch). Complete bikes shipped with both stems, so check the box first.

evidence.says: Spec lists two Trinity alloy stems: zero stack and +30 mm stack.

Owner estimates about 25 mm height difference between high and low stems; TT owners add stack with longer aftermarket bolts.

evidence.says: After a cracked bar on a 2017 Pro, an owner answers that only Giant bars fit, though any extensions can be used.
Owner: the base-bar fitting is proprietary; another bar would only fit if its holes lined up exactly.
Owner: the non-Pro Trinity Advanced has a standard stem/base-bar clamp and can take a full Profile Design cockpit; Pro owners are limited to parts changes.
Owner: the Pro has an integrated stem/bar/fork while the 2016 non-Pro uses a traditional stem and alloy bars.
Pro TT owner: proprietary base-bar mounting means other base bars are not usable.

gaps: Giant's own Trinity Advanced Pro manual (Version 9/2015, with armrest reach and fork steerer tables) could only be seen as search excerpts: manualmachine.com and manuals.online returned 403. The '4 positions x reversible = 5 fore-aft positions, 15 mm steps, 60 mm' reach description comes from a search excerpt of that manual.

Pad stack/reach reference point is not stated anywhere for this generation, so stock_range uses 'unspecified'. Giant's tables also conflict: the 2018 and 2021 complete-bike pages give one range per size (stack XS 550-600, S 580-630, M 610-660, L 640-690; reach XS 443-503, S 455-515, M 462-532, L 468-538), which matches the 2022 TT stack but is about 50 mm longer in reach than the 2022 TT reach (403-463 ... 428-488). Likely a different reference point; not resolved.

Extension and base-bar clamp diameters for the Pro cockpit are not published; owners fitted standard round aftermarket extensions (Zipp, PD, D2Z, Carbon Wasp, Kismet) but no source states 22.2 mm for the Trinity clamps. One owner measured the base-bar ends at ~22.7 mm (SRAM Blip Grip clamps did not fit).

Which aftermarket armrests bolt directly onto the stock clamps: only a 30 mm bolt-spacing measurement and a Profile Design F35 suggestion exist; earlier research note that PD F40/Boom fit could not be re-verified.

One 2017 owner fitted a Deda Kronos Due base bar and another later fitted/bought a Profile Design Aeria cockpit, but neither post confirms the bike was a Pro (not the standard-stem non-Pro) or that it mounted; left out.
No maker product pages found for FastTT (only retailer copies of the maker text), Fouriers (only eBay listings, which returned 403), D2Z or Carbon Wasp Trinity compatibility.
Revolverwheels (UK) Trinity wedges and Aerocoach 'Angles' extensions were each mentioned once without a fit result; not listed.
